name: Chapel of the Transfiguration
summary: An exterior-only Western Craftsman landmark using the named chapel footprint as the authoritative runtime placement and the nearby named Brides' Room footprint as restrained immediate companion massing.

included: attached chapel projections visible from outside
excluded: pews, altar, pulpit, and other interior furnishings
bell canopy and storage shed until their footprints are independently resolved

structures.name: Chapel of the Transfiguration Brides' Room

placement.strategy: Select the two exact named records, retain their polygon vertices without buffering or rectangular replacement, and preserve their relative placement. Re-resolve by exact name and compare the source-file hash before every deterministic rebuild.

selector.name: Chapel of the Transfiguration Brides' Room

resolution_steps: Hash terrain/public/buildings.json and persist the hash in the run artifact.
Resolve exactly one record for each exact-name selector; reject zero or multiple matches.
Compare resolved vertices, source heights, and relative centroids with this package snapshot.
Use the current terrain sampler for ground elevation and re-basing; never bake an assumed absolute elevation.
Confirm the chapel axis and southeast-facing approach against the National Register description before capture approval.

budgets.material_policy: Share compact log, wood-shake, dark trim, and board-and-batten material families. A registered projection is permitted only on exterior chapel surfaces and must not encode an interior view.

lods.intent: Recognizable log ends, spear-ended fascia silhouette, measured exterior openings, shake roof character, and restrained ground contact.
Retain the long low nave, primary and projecting gables, altar-window opening, and separate Brides' Room mass.
Preserve the chapel's axial gable silhouette, principal wall/roof split, and companion footprint only.

required_views.purpose: Entrance door, projecting gables, fascia treatment, and public approach.
Horizontal log courses, lattice casement rhythm, log corners, and shake roof.
Exterior scale and framing of the signature fixed-sash altar-window opening; the interior mountain view is excluded.

prompt_constraints: Preserve the exact registered target silhouette, roof topology, openings, crop, camera, and transparent/background mask.
Use only references proven to depict the Chapel of the Transfiguration or its named Brides' Room; exclude the Chapel of the Sacred Heart and other rustic chapels.
Keep the chapel a long, low Western Craftsman lodgepole-log building with moderate wood-shake gables and smaller documented projecting gables.

Preserve sawn log ends beyond the corners, spear-ended raking fascias, the beveled vertical-plank entrance door, lattice casements, and the fixed-sash altar-window opening where geometry establishes them.
Do not infer geometry, dimensions, placement, roof pitches, openings, or additions from image generation.

Do not generate a view through the building, an interior, pews, altar furnishings, stained glass, religious figures, people, vehicles, signs, text, watermarks, landscape, mountains, sky, featureless black rectangles, or baked cast shadows.
Keep tileable materials free of perspective, vegetation, sky, and directional sunlight.

checks: single-candidate geometry, draw-call, and texture budgets
one active LOD for the combined landmark
projection registration at frontal and grazing angles
closed exterior envelope with no walkable interior or portal
no production asset or manifest mutation

conditions: The chapel lacks an official NPS identity and architectural source.
Fewer than two useful, same-building exterior elevations have item-level creator and rights metadata before projection.
Any acquired artifact lacks final URL, creator, rights statement, retrieval date, byte count, and SHA-256.
A visual reference may show the Chapel of the Sacred Heart or another rustic chapel.
Either exact named footprint is absent or non-unique.
Any vertex or relative-center drift exceeds 0.25 metres without an approved source migration.
The chapel axis or southeast-facing relationship conflicts with the National Register description.
The main chapel is not traceable to the documented approximately 22 by 50 foot massing and named footprint.
Documented gable projections, sacristy relationship, or signature fascia silhouette are lost in a required LOD.
Image generation determines dimensions, roof topology, placement, or openings.
Roofs intersect walls incorrectly, daylight gaps appear, or foundations float.
Projection edges drift from the approved orthographic target.
Black placeholder openings, an invented interior view, landscape baked into the facade, cross-building contamination, or unsupported religious ornament is visible.
Vegetation or fence clearing extends beyond physical access and envelope clearance.
Any LOD, material-primitive, or texture budget is exceeded.
More than one landmark LOD is active.
The required capture suite reports console errors, failed asset requests, or unacceptable frame-time regression.

promotion.reason: This package is draft-only. Promotion requires separate user approval for this named candidate.
